fixes.explanation: Comfort is a tempting pick, friend. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer on a pile of paper and dust, and I know the appeal of a soft landing. But the writer doesn't list it. The verse says to pursue peace with everyone, as well as holiness.

Yes, a single meal. The writer says Esau “…for a single meal sold his birthright.” Genesis 25:34 says Jacob gave him bread and lentil stew. That's one meal, baker. A birthright is a LOT to trade for a bowl of stew.
Egypt is a big name in the Bible, friend, but it isn't here. The writer says the congregation of the firstborn is “…enrolled in heaven.” That's the word that fills the blank.

True, baker. The writer says you have come to “…the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.” Abel was killed by his brother Cain (Genesis 4:8), and God told Cain, “Your brother's blood cries out to Me from the ground” (Genesis 4:10). So both bloods speak, and the writer says one speaks better.

That's true, friend. The writer says the sprinkled blood “…speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.” Abel's blood cried out from the ground (Genesis 4:10). The writer sets the two side by side and says the sprinkled blood speaks the better word.

Yes, baker. The writer says, “…how much less will we escape if we reject Him who warns us from heaven?” So the people did not escape when they refused Him on earth, and the writer says it's even less for us if we reject Him from heaven. That's a serious line, and it's worth sitting with.
